newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Workers block roads in Romania labour unrest.
newsitem.headline: Workers block roads in Romania labour unrest.

text.p: Thousands of workers at a big truck plant north of Bucharest blocked roads on Tuesday in the latest in a series of protests denouncing Romania's market reforms.

Workers at the state-run Roman SA truck maker in Brasov had returned from a week's layoff because of a lack of orders to find power had been cut to workshops because of half a million dollars in unpaid electricity bills.

"Our jobs are insecure, our salaries are unpaid and we fear the factory could be closed down altogether," union leader Gheorghe Marmalichi said by telephone from the city, 160 km (100 miles) north of the capital.
Trade unionists, estimated at 6,000 by police, blocked a main road into Brasov through the evening and refused to move even after the arrival of a team of government negotiators.
Once a successful plant, Roman and its 13,800 employees now produce only a fraction of communist-era output.
Workers in a broad series of industries have launched limited protests against the new centrist government's drive to cut spending and subsidies to loss-making industries.
Thousands of coal miners stopped work for two hours last week to protest against the reforms. Energy and communications workers have staged brief protests in Bucharest against proposed privatisation.
